summary: Iteration 5 — verified kernel v3 wrap end-to-end, focusing on Grok's must-fix owed-pact regression. Backend: 33/33 pytest pass (11 new in test_kernel_owed_pact.py + 22 regression across test_kernel_diplomacy.py and test_kernel_persistence.py). NEW E2E OWED-PACT FLOW proven with a real accepted trade: (1) 2-human + 1-AI game via create-game + join-game + /start; (2) inbox response shape confirmed to include kernel v3 fields `owedDeliveries` and `allyIds` (all arrays); (3) Alice POSTs /diplomacy/send trade {give: tech:1, request: chon:1} to Bob with valid giveSystemId/requestSystemId picked from tradeFrontier-eligible landing systems; (4) Bob POSTs /diplomacy/accept on the open message; (5) GET /diplomacy/inbox/{alice} returns owedDeliveries=[{pactId, resources:{tech:1,...}, systemId, otherId:bob}] — non-empty, real resources, matching Grok's spec exactly; (6) symmetric check: Bob's inbox also shows owed chon:1; (7) POST /diplomacy/deliver-pact with the real pactId returns 200 status:ok (this is the previously-untested happy path Grok flagged); (8) bogus pact_id still returns 400 with kernel-derived detail; (9) after deliver, Alice's owed row is cleared/removed; (10) kernel CLI ping returns {ok:true,pong:true,version:3}; (11) persistence roundtrip regression: create → GET state → `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` → re-GET state shows same system IDs. Frontend: root URL loads Consilium Mundi lobby with ZERO console errors and ZERO page errors. Lobby dropdown [data-testid=landing-num-players] has EXACTLY two options — value=3 '3–4 admiralties (open seats fill with AI)' and value=4 '4 admiralties'. No '2 players' string present. No import errors for MapCanvas/OrdersTray/ResourceHUD.
critical_code_review_comments: ObligationsHUD.jsx correctly consumes inbox.owedDeliveries and filters via nonEmptyResources — the pact.a.playerId bug Grok flagged is fully gone.
kernel_api.py inbox route (line 548-559) passes through owedDeliveries + allyIds cleanly; contract with host.ts::inboxForPlayer is aligned.

MapCanvas.jsx and OrdersTray.jsx are honest scaffolds that return null with TODO comments — safe placeholders, no runtime impact. App.js still owns renderGalaxyMap/renderOrdersPanel until the follow-up split.
ResourceHUD.jsx is a clean 14-line extraction with proper null-guard; App.js consumes it via the top-bar (resource-hud testid).
Persistence path (_persist -> asyncio.get_running_loop -> create_task) already logs DAO errors — no regression from iter 4.
